title: Delegated approval authority and need-to-know visibility
description:
Phase 6. Blocked by the collaboration epic, because this should be built against a running multi-member organization rather than in the abstract. The design risk of the whole initiative lives here.

Modeled on an office. Every member holds an authority ceiling; no one can grant, approve, or always-allow beyond it; roles are named ceilings rather than a permission matrix; delegation clips and expires. Ceilings are argument-bound, not class-bound: approving a copy edit and approving a production publication are both publish, and the target separates them.

**Order inside the epic:** 24df70 specifies, then eef4aa lands alone because everything depends on it, then ac3b7a, b49a89, and 14cf05 in parallel, then e4053a last.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Ceilings are argument-bound, not class-bound. Approving a copy edit and approving a production publication are both publish; the target separates them. A ceiling therefore has the shape TaskCapabilityGrant already uses (action types with argument constraints, origins, recipients, file scopes, egress classes, spend limit), which makes a ceiling a grant a member holds standing rather than one a task receives. Clipping is set intersection on those fields for delegation, rules, grants, and approvals alike.

Also in scope: the five consequential classes are an egress taxonomy inherited from a household. Ingesting a reference is approval-worthy in an organization and is the primary attack in the threat model, so ingest must become a class a ceiling can bound, not only a grant field.
